componentPlan.focusQuote: Compound interest is when you earn interest on both the money you save and the interest you earn.
componentPlan.pedagogicalReason: Models the lump sum example so learners see interest earning interest over time.

componentPlan.focusQuote: Post-secondary education: Includes all forms of schooling after high school, not just college.
componentPlan.pedagogicalReason: Checks recall of saving vocabulary and reasons for starting early to pay education costs.

overview.headline: Saving early lets compound interest grow money for college costs

keyPoints.point: Starting saving sooner helps money grow faster for post-secondary education through compound interest.
keyPoints.quote: The sooner you start saving for post-secondary education, the faster your money can grow from compound interest.

keyPoints.point: Compound interest means you earn interest on both the money you save and the interest you earn.
keyPoints.quote: Compound interest is when you earn interest on both the money you save and the interest you earn.

keyPoints.point: To invest principal that earns percent interest shows how compounding frequency shapes growth over year.
keyPoints.quote: So let's say you invest $1,000 (your principal) and it earns 5 percent (interest rate) once a year (the compounding frequency).

keyPoints.point: First year growth shows original principal plus percent interest building savings over time.
keyPoints.quote: After the first year, you would have $1,050—your original principal, plus 5 percent, or $50.

keyTerms.gloss: interest earned on saved money and on previously earned interest
keyTerms.quote: Compound interest is when you earn interest on both the money you save and the interest you earn.

keyTerms.gloss: percentage charged for borrowed money or paid on saved deposits
keyTerms.quote: Interest rate: A percentage of a sum borrowed that is charged by a lender or merchant for letting you use its money.

keyTerms.gloss: starting amount you invest that earns interest over time
keyTerms.quote: So let's say you invest $1,000 (your principal) and it earns 5 percent (interest rate) once a year (the compounding frequency).

keyTerms.gloss: how often interest is added to savings during the year
keyTerms.quote: Increasing the compounding frequency or your interest rate or adding to your principal can help your savings grow even faster.
